customManagers.description: The Python base image is written twice: in serve_api/Dockerfile and in the deps-linux target of serve_api/Makefile, which compiles the hashed requirements on the same image. The Dockerfile is found by the docker manager; this entry finds the Makefile copy under the same depName and datasource, so both move in one pull request. The requirements are not recompiled by this change: a Python minor bump needs them recompiled on the new image (make deps-linux ARGS=--upgrade) and pushed onto the pull request.

packageRules.description: Runner image majors move deliberately, in one pull request for all workflows.
Major updates wait in the Dependency Dashboard until someone approves them.

description: ICTU recommendation 7: do not take a new major's first release. Renovate
never proposes X.0.0 for a PyPI package, so the earliest a major can be
offered is X.0.1 — the first patch, by which point the release has been
used by others. Majors still wait for Dependency Dashboard approval as
well (the rule above): this decides WHICH version may be offered, that
one decides WHETHER it is raised at all, and the assessment R7 asks for is
what the person ticking the box is doing.
allowedVersions applies to every update type of a matched package, not
only majors, which is why the pattern is written to match X.0.0 alone: no
minor or patch release can look like that. Scoped to the pypi datasource
deliberately — the same pattern against Docker tags (3.14-bookworm) or
the github-runner datasource (ubuntu 26.04) would mean something else
The cost, stated plainly: a package that publishes X.0.0 and never a patch
is never offered that major. Add a per-package exception with the reason,
the way a deferral is recorded.
minimumReleaseAge repeats the top-level 14 days and changes nothing; it is
here because Semgrep's renovate-missing-minimum-release-age flags a rule
that does not set it locally.

packageRules.description: Python minor and major moves are one pull request (Dockerfile, Makefile image and the workflows' python-version) and only on approval, so the image and the CI Python stay together.
Lock-file maintenance moves the transitive tree, so it is prioritised within the normal pull request limit.
